The approved product consists of a plasmid DNA encoding two viral antigens, delivered by intramuscular injection followed by electroporation. In a randomized, placebo-controlled trial of 198 adults with recurrent respiratory papillomatosis, the proportion requiring surgery in the 12 months after treatment was 31 percent in the treatment arm versus 62 percent in the placebo arm (relative risk 0.50; 95% CI 0.33 to 0.75). Common adverse reactions included injection site pain, muscle ache, and fever. The prescribing information advises that patients may develop antibodies against the plasmid, with unknown clinical significance. Dose is 1 mg administered at weeks 0, 4, and 12, then a booster at week 52. Use is contraindicated in patients with a history of severe reaction to any component.
